title: Courses · Objectives / Outcomes / Requirements
intro: Refero evidence for structured objectives, learner visibility, requirements, downstream links, authoring guidance, and course setup sequencing.

questions.title: Objectives are structured (list items, not free text) and reorderable
Objectives are visible to the learner in the same shape the instructor authored them
Requirements / prerequisites are enforced or only informational (and how that's communicated)
Objectives can be linked downstream (lesson, assessment, competency)
Guidance for authoring (examples, verb prompts, character limits, AI suggestions)
Where in the course-creation flow this step sits (required up front vs. optional later)

references.title: Course outline creation interface
references.question: Q1
references.take: The course outline screen presents curriculum content as a navigable authored structure with a dedicated creation surface, supporting structured course building rather than one free-text field.

references.title: Choose curriculum method with AI option
references.question: Q5
references.take: The outline method screen visibly offers a Generate with AI choice and a course-description input, providing authoring guidance through a concrete generation path.

references.title: Course setup guide and curriculum checklist
references.question: Q2
references.take: The setup guide provides the course title and curriculum in a learner-facing course context, useful evidence for checking whether authored expectations are surfaced consistently.

references.title: Course metadata step with gated Continue
references.question: Q6
references.take: The first wizard screen captures title and description before later setup, and its Continue action is disabled until required metadata is present.

references.title: Completed course metadata step
references.question: Q3
references.take: The completed metadata state shows progression to the next setup step without a visible prerequisite control; prerequisite enforcement therefore remains unverified from this evidence.

references.title: Learner course overview with progress
references.question: Q2
references.take: The learner course screen presents a named module, progress percentage, and Continue action in a compact course-card shape, showing how course expectations can remain visible in the learning surface.

references.title: Goals list with connected projects
references.question: Q4
references.take: The goals view explicitly shows connected projects and their progress under a goal, demonstrating a downstream link from an outcome to supporting work.

references.title: Goal detail with sub-goal and project references
references.question: Q4
references.take: The goal detail screen exposes progress, a Connect a sub-goal action, and references to projects or portfolios, making hierarchy and traceability explicit.

references.title: Product planning with initiatives and projects
references.question: Q4
references.take: Linear’s planning surface describes aligning projects under larger goals and mapping dependencies, a useful comparison for preserving objective-to-work relationships.

references.title: Objective selection during onboarding
references.question: Q5
references.take: Asana’s onboarding asks the user to choose a main objective from labeled options with short explanations, showing lightweight guidance before deeper goal authoring.

references.title: Create and publish course wizard
references.question: Q6
references.take: The observed 34-step flow starts with a five-step metadata and pricing wizard, then chooses an outline method and builds curriculum before publishing, so objectives are introduced after initial course details rather than at the first screen.
